Analyzing categorical time series with the R package ctsfeatures
summary: Most time-series methodology targets real-valued data, leaving categorical time series without a broad R toolkit for feature extraction and exploratory analysis. The paper presents ctsfeatures, which implements marginal and serial-dependence features, visualization tools, packaged biological and synthetic datasets, and examples of classification, clustering and outlier detection. In the GeneticSequences example, the distance-based outlier score and boxplot flag two sequences as anomalous, while other examples report high classification accuracy and clustering ARI.

"""Download the ctsfeatures CRAN source tarball into the shared data cache and extract it."""
import os
import re
import sys
import tarfile
import urllib.request

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join("data"))
CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"


def pkg_version(name="ctsfeatures"):
    url = f"{CRAN}/src/contrib/PACKAGES"
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as r:
        txt = r.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    # PACKAGES is DCF: blocks separated by blank lines
    for block in txt.split("\n\n"):
        lines = block.splitlines()
        if lines and lines[0].strip() == f"Package: {name}":
            for ln in lines:
                if ln.startswith("Version:"):
                    return ln.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    raise RuntimeError(f"{name} not found in PACKAGES index")


def main():
    os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    ver = pkg_version()
    fn = f"ctsfeatures_{ver}.tar.gz"
    path = os.path.join(CACHE, fn)
    if not os.path.exists(path) or os.path.getsize(path) < 10000:
        url = f"{CRAN}/src/contrib/{fn}"
        print("downloading", url)
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, path)
    else:
        print("cached", path)
    outdir = os.path.join(CACHE, "ctsfeatures_src")
    marker = os.path.join(outdir, "ctsfeatures", "R")
    if not os.path.isdir(marker):
        with tarfile.open(path, "r:gz") as tf:
            tf.extractall(outdir)
    print("version", ver)
    print("src", os.path.join(outdir, "ctsfeatures"))
    return ver


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Locate and download the ctsfeatures CRAN source tarball (with mirrors + GitHub fallbacks)."""
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import tarfile
import urllib.request
import urllib.error

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", "data")

CANDIDATES = [
    "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/ctsfeatures_0.2.1.tar.gz",
    "https://mirror.las.iastate.edu/CRAN/src/contrib/ctsfeatures_0.2.1.tar.gz",
    "https://cran.us.r-project.org/src/contrib/ctsfeatures_0.2.1.tar.gz",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/ctsfeatures_0.2.1.tar.gz",
    "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/ctsfeatures/ctsfeatures_0.2.1.tar.gz",
]
IDX = [
    "https://mirror.las.iastate.edu/CRAN/src/contrib/PACKAGES",
    "https://cran.us.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES",
    "https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES",
]


def fetch(url, timeout=120):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "python-urllib/ctsfeatures-repro"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
        return r.read()


def version_from_index():
    for u in IDX:
        try:
            txt = fetch(u).decode("utf-8", "replace")
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            print("index fail", u, e)
            continue
        for block in txt.split("\n\n"):
            lines = block.splitlines()
            if lines and lines[0].strip() == "Package: ctsfeatures":
                for ln in lines:
                    if ln.startswith("Version:"):
                        return ln.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
    return None


def main():
    os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    ver = version_from_index()
    print("index version:", ver)
    if ver:
        fn = f"ctsfeatures_{ver}.tar.gz"
        CANDIDATES.insert(0, f"https://mirror.las.iastate.edu/CRAN/src/contrib/{fn}")
        CANDIDATES.insert(0, f"https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/{fn}")
        CANDIDATES.insert(0, f"https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/{fn}")
    dest = None
    for url in CANDIDATES:
        fn = os.path.basename(url)
        p = os.path.join(CACHE, fn)
        if os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p) > 20000:
            print("cached", p)
            dest = p
            break
        try:
            print("try", url)
            blob = fetch(url)
            if len(blob) < 20000:
                raise RuntimeError("too small")
            with open(p, "wb") as f:
                f.write(blob)
            print("ok", p, len(blob))
            dest = p
            break
        except Exception as e:  # noqa
            print("  fail:", e)
            time.sleep(1)
    if dest is None:
        raise SystemExit("could not download ctsfeatures source")
    outdir = os.path.join(CACHE, "ctsfeatures_src")
    marker = os.path.join(outdir, "ctsfeatures", "R")
    if not os.path.isdir(marker):
        with tarfile.open(dest, "r:gz") as tf:
            tf.extractall(outdir)
    print("SRC:", os.path.join(outdir, "ctsfeatures"))
    print("FILES:")
    root = os.path.join(outdir, "ctsfeatures")
    for dirpath, _dirs, files in os.walk(root):
        for f in files:
            print(" ", os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), root))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#' Computes the marginal probabilities of a categorical time series
#'
#' \code{marginal_probabilities} returns a vector with the marginal
#' probabilities of a categorical time series
#'
#' @param series An object of type \code{tsibble} (see R package \code{tsibble}), whose column named Value
#' contains the values of the corresponding CTS. This column must be of class \code{factor} and its levels
#' must be determined by the range of the CTS.
#' @return A vector with the marginal probabilities.
#' @examples
#' sequence_1 <- GeneticSequences[which(GeneticSequences$Series==1),]
#' vector_mp <- marginal_probabilities(series = sequence_1) # Computing the vector of
#' # marginal probabilities for the first series in dataset GeneticSequences
#' @details
#' Given a CTS of length \eqn{T} with range \eqn{\mathcal{V}=\{1, 2, \ldots, r\}},
#' \eqn{\overline{X}_t=\{\overline{X}_1,\ldots, \overline{X}_T\}}, the function computes the
#' vector \eqn{\widehat{\boldsymbol p} =(\widehat{p}_1, \ldots, \widehat{p}_r)},
#' with \eqn{\widehat{p}_i=\frac{N_i}{T}}, where \eqn{N_i} is the number
#' of elements equal to \eqn{i} in the realization \eqn{\overline{X}_t}.
#' @encoding UTF-8
#' @author
#' Ángel López-Oriona, José A. Vilar
#' @references{
#'
#'   \insertRef{weiss2008measuring}{ctsfeatures}
#'
#' }
#' @export

marginal_probabilities <- function(series) {

  check_cts(series)
  series_length <- length(series$Value) # Series length
  categories <- levels(series$Value)
  n_cat <- length(categories) # Number of categories in the dataset


  # Computing the marginal probabilities in the series

  marginal_probabilities <- numeric()

  for (i in 1 : n_cat) {

    count_i <- sum(series$Value == categories[[i]])
    marginal_probabilities[i] <- count_i/series_length

  }

  return(marginal_probabilities)

}

    root = os.path.join(CACHE, f"ctsfeatures_src_{PKG_VERSION.replace('.', '_')}")

audit_summary: The C1 target was reproduced with the actual packaged GeneticSequences data: the port reads ctsfeatures 1.0.0's .RData, computes lag-1 psi_ij and marginal probabilities, concatenates them, applies Euclidean dist() and colSums(), and uses boxplot(range=1). The clean rerun gives top-2 scores 9.8359 and 9.6331, upper whisker 9.1842, and exactly indices 7 and 10 flagged, so value=2. No paper number is hardcoded; the target value is recomputed from the generated CSV, and the zero diagonal is included exactly as colSums(as.matrix(dist_db)) would. All 32 series are used with L=1, so there is no scale-down. The extra C2 check also returns 2; C3/C4 were not part of the selected match target. The only caveat is that R was unavailable, so the R functions were ported to Python from the package source, but the formulas match the paper's configured pipeline.

requirement_check.evidence: reproduce.py loads GeneticSequences.RData from ctsfeatures 1.0.0 via rdata; fallback_c1.run_c1 asserts n=32, checks alphabet {a,c,g,t}, reports n_classes=4, class counts, and variable series lengths; clean rerun feature matrix is 32x20.

fallback_c1 uses one fixed category vector CATS_C1=['a','g','c','t'] for all 32 series in binarization, marginal probabilities, and psi features; category-order sensitivity is checked by rerunning with ['a','c','g','t'] and returns identical outlier scores.

total_correlation_features binarizes each series and computes the full r x r Pearson-correlation matrix for lag 1; feature_row exposes the individual psi_ij(1) terms rather than only an aggregate sum.
marginal_probabilities computes p_i as the observed count of category i divided by sequence length T; these four probabilities are appended to every feature row.

feature_row concatenates the lag-1 psi_ij terms and marginal probabilities, and distance_dB computes Euclidean distance, i.e. the square root of squared psi and p differences. For the paper's configured L=1 case this matches the cbind(...) + dist() dB pipeline; no multi-lag loop is exercised because L=1.
LAG=1 in fallback_c1; the clean rerun uses exactly one lag for both C1 and the extra C2 check.
feature_matrix stacks cbind-style rows of psi terms plus marginal probabilities; distance_dB forms the full pairwise Euclidean distance matrix without scaling, matching dist(data_db).
outlier_pipeline computes outlier_score = dist_db.sum(axis=0), equivalent to colSums(as.matrix(dist_db)); the zero diagonal is included, as in the paper, and does not affect ranking.

boxplot_stats uses type-7 quartiles and coefficient range=1, then flags scores strictly above the upper whisker. The clean rerun gives upper whisker 9.1842 and flags exactly the two series with scores 9.8359 and 9.6331.
run_c1 computes outlier scores without using GeneticSequences$classes; class labels are only written to the output CSV for post-hoc inspection, and no supervised classifier is fitted.
